No skill step codifies it, but O14–O16 (PR review), O17–O26 (audit-025) and O45 (BK-504 table check) were all written outside /observe-review, each group opened by a source line.

options.label: Write O92, O93 now (Recommended)
options.description: This session appends them to Open items, following the audit-025/O45 precedent, with a source line naming the reopen under RFC-0030 C4 (no BK-511 IDs). O92 in reopen shape (D6 conflicts with itself and D155), O93 as a gap in D18. Phase B's /observe walks them directly; the full /observe-review re-run follows per RFC-0030 C3.

options.label: /observe-review OP-01 records
options.description: List both as candidates in BK-485's dossier (the O27–O44 channel) and run a full /observe-review first, which verifies and writes them. Costs an extra full review before the reopen, and that review may add more items that then also block freeze-2.

questions.question: Which freeze tag is BK-506's faithfulness trial subject? Its trial is not pre-registered yet, so RFC-0029 R2's 'keeps that tag' clause does not bind it.

options.label: freeze-2 (Recommended)
options.description: The trial's oracles are written from a record without the two known blocking gaps. BK-506's entry names freeze-2; its Stage 0 dry run can still go ahead, but the run waits for the reopen, review and tag.

options.label: freeze-1
options.description: The trial can start now on a7de4e31, but its E oracles meet two behaviours the record leaves two-valued or undecided, so seeded misreadings touching read(0) or the last-byte read cannot be scored cleanly.

OP-01 has four items blocking freeze-2 from this review: O94 and O95 reopen D158, O96 reopens D51, O97 is a gap in D152. O98 to O101 are notes. Since RFC-0031 merged, freeze-2 must also re-witness O29, O42, O76 and O88 without 0.33 code, and only a reopen does that. How should they be resolved?

options.label: One reopen for all (Recommended)
options.description: Run /observe OP-01 in a fresh session. It walks O94 to O97 with full option dialogs, routes notes O98 to O101, and re-witnesses O29, O42, O76 and O88 against the SDK, OS or runtime. Then one /observe-review. A single review pass, and O94 (end detection on Local and SFTP) gets a real dialog.

options.label: Close-out, then reopen
options.description: /observe-review OP-01 close-out now settles O94 to O101 in one dialog, recommended answers first (RFC-0030 C2). A reopen still has to re-witness the four 0.33-sourced items, followed by its own review. Two passes before freeze-2.

options.label: Stop here
options.description: Leave the branch at fdbadf9 with O94 to O101 open. Freeze-2 and BK-506 wait.

OP-01/O94 (AX-6, Exhausted on Local and SFTP): a stream over a 10-byte file returns all ten bytes; O3 may then append two (E4). D158 says the next read makes no backend contact, D26 says the read ends at the end it meets. Which holds on file-system backends?

options.label: Stop at open length (Recommended)
options.description: Every backend: Exhausted once delivered bytes reach the length fixed at open (D22), no contact after. Appended bytes are never delivered; a truncation under E4 still ends early where a read meets it (D99). D26 reads 'ends at the earlier of the end it meets and the length fixed at open'. No new variation point. Source: D22, D158; HTTP Content-Length.

options.label: Read on to the end
options.description: On Local and SFTP the read after the last byte contacts the backend (read(2), CMD_READ), may fail (Failed) or be cancelled, and delivers appended bytes. D158's 'no backend contact' holds on object stores only: a new D43 variation point. Source: POSIX read(2), io.

options.label: Unspecified on FS
options.description: On file-system backends the read after the last byte returns appended bytes, b'', or a stream-read failure, which one unspecified; a check accepts all three. Weakest promise, no implementation constraint.

questions.question: OP-01/O95 (AX-6 vs NP2): D158 says a read on an Exhausted stream makes 'no backend contact'; NP2 leaves every request count unpromised, and a test asserting one is a defect (D41). What does D158 promise?

options.label: Outcome only (Recommended)
options.description: D158 promises the outcome: the end value (D132), failing only with a caller error (D51), a cancellation to Closed (D50). Its request count is NP2's; 'no backend contact' becomes the reason, not a promise. NP2 keeps one scope. Source: D41 option (a) as D107 restores it.

options.label: Zero requests
options.description: D158 promises no backend request on an Exhausted read; NP2's scope gains 'except a read on an Exhausted stream'. A test may count requests there, and NP2 carries a carve-out.

questions.question: OP-01/O96 (AX-6): on an Open stream the caller calls seek(0), catches io.UnsupportedOperation, then read(3). D51 sends every failure but a caller error or cancellation to Failed. What state follows an unsupported method?

options.label: State unchanged (Recommended)
options.description: An unsupported method (D153's row) raises before any effect and leaves every state as it was, as a caller error does; read(3) returns the next bytes. D51 reads 'every failure but a caller error, an unsupported method and a cancellation'; D153's own category stays apart. Source: io.BufferedReader (run in O96), D70, D125, D151.

options.label: Moves to Failed
options.description: D51 as written: seek(0) on an Open stream makes it Failed, every later data read re-raising io.UnsupportedOperation (D52). Breaks io-contract code that probes seek; D151 and D125 amended to match.

questions.question: OP-01/O97 (AX-4, gap): on an SFTP server running Windows, an AsyncStore task awaiting a stream read is cancelled; the stream is Closed (D20) while the worker thread still holds the server's file handle, and O2 replaces the item. Does D138's deviation and D10's exception (D152) reach it?

options.label: Yes, widen both (Recommended)
options.description: D138's deviation covers a cancelled stream read as well as a cancelled close: the point is renamed 'Cancelled release' and O13 reads so. D10's exception reads 'a stream whose release a cancellation left pending'; NP5's SFTP example likewise. Source: D138, D152, asyncio.to_thread (run in O76); server not run.

options.label: Shield the read
options.description: On such a backend a cancelled read waits for its worker's read and close before propagating, so no release is pending and D10 stays as D152 set it. Cancellation late by the read's duration, unlike D138's close.
